headings.text: Tokens (JWT) when a cert isn't convenient
Building a product integration (vs. a user client)

blocks.html:
This is the concrete flow for obtaining the mTLS client certificate (and, where needed, a JWT) that authenticates you to TAK Server on a Deploy App deployment. The operations are in the Deploy App Core API (RASENMAEHER) spec under /api/v1/….

The human flow first

Deploy App's onboarding is invite-and-approve:

  1. An operator stands up the stack and creates the first admin. Bootstrapping uses a one-time code — rasenmaeher_api addcode on the server, paired with the GET /api/v1/firstuser/check-code and POST /api/v1/firstuser/add-admin endpoints.
  2. Admins invite users — invite codes and verification codes: POST /api/v1/enrollment/invitecode/create, POST /api/v1/enrollment/generate-verification-code.
  3. A user enrolls with that code: POST /api/v1/enrollment/init, then polls GET /api/v1/enrollment/have-i-been-accepted / …/status.
  4. An admin approves the waiting user: POST /api/v1/enrollment/accept (admins can also promote / demote / lock).

Once accepted, the identity becomes certificate-backed.

Getting the certificate (CSR signing)

Your client (or service) generates a key pair and a CSR, and Deploy App's CA signs it:

  • POST /api/v1/product/sign_csr — submit a CSR, get back the signed client certificate and the CA chain.
  • POST /api/v1/product/sign_csr/mtls — the mTLS-authenticated variant (renew/issue when you already hold a cert).
  • POST /api/v1/product/renew_csr — renew before expiry.
  • POST /api/v1/product/revoke/mtls — revoke.

The returned certificate + CA chain is exactly what you load into your TLS client to present to TAK Server (Marti API and the CoT stream) and to Keycloak.

Tokens (JWT) when a cert isn't convenient

For flows that use a bearer token instead of (or alongside) the cert:

  • POST /api/v1/token/jwt/exchange — exchange a credential for a JWT.
  • GET /api/v1/token/jwt/refresh — refresh it.
  • POST /api/v1/token/code/generate + POST /api/v1/token/code/exchange — the login-code pattern (generate a short code, exchange it for a token) used by UI/device onboarding.

Verify whichever you hold with the check-auth endpoints: /api/v1/check-auth/mtls, /check-auth/jwt, /check-auth/mtls_or_jwt, /check-auth/validuser.

Building a product integration (vs. a user client)

If you're registering a new product/service with Deploy App (not just connecting as a user), the core also exposes a product proxy (/api/v1/product/proxy/<short_name>/…) and an outbound callback contract — the hub calls your integration over mTLS on every user change so you stay in sync. That side is its own topic (Deploy App's Build an Integration book); for talking to TAK Server you typically just need the client certificate above.

Full request/response shapes are in the Deploy App Core API reference (public/api-specs/rasenmaeher/). Treat the endpoint names here as the map; the spec is the territory.
